parts.text: An IGCSE class is carrying out this experiment to determine the mass of a metal block. Fig. 1.1 shows a spring drawn full size. Fig. 1.2, also full size, shows the spring with a load of 100 g suspended from it. Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) On Fig. 1.1, measure the length l 0 , in cm, of the spring without any load. l 0 = ................................................. cm

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the extension e 1 of the spring using the equation e 1 = ( l 1 – l 0 ). e 1 = ..................................................[1]

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Determine a value for k using the equation k = m e 1 , where m = 100 g. k = ........................ unit ...................[2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The apparatus is then set up as shown in Fig. 1.3. The rule is at a small angle to the bench. Fig. 1.3 A student measures the length of the stretched spring and obtains the result 4.4 cm l 2 = ......................................................

ms.label: 1(b)(i)
ms.text: e.g. measure half width of mass either side of 40 cm/mark centre of mass

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student measures the new length l 3 of the spring and records it as 7.5 cm l 3 = ...................................................... Determine the change in the extension e 2 due to block X , using the equation e 2 = ( l 3 – l 2 ). e 2 = ......................................................

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the mass M of block X using your answers to (a)(iv) and (b)(ii) and the equation M = k e 2 0.40 . M = ...................................................[2]
